## The Payload — Forced Incompatibilities

*Section 8 of the seed: the combinations of target properties proven incompatible by survived challenge, not asserted.*

- **[HARD] Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs) ✕ Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs), Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land), Ownership semantics without GC, derived from the proof layer*
  - surfaced by: Memory model — what replaces Rust's borrow checker (linear types, region inference, or something derived from the proof layer)?
  - Decidable proof-free checking collides with a seamless ownership layer over weak-memory aliasing — The mandatory bare-metal domain — lock-free/publishing atomics, MMIO, DMA, n-reader sharing — has ownership that is dynamic or externally driven, not structural, so typing it soundly under weak memory requires transferable protocol invariants (the RustBelt/GPS/iRC11 machinery). Such invariants cannot be inferred inside a decidable, zero-annotation, finite-height/quantifier-free fragment: the moment the lattice is expressive enough to name them, the join-point/loop merge of the heap becomes bi-abduction (Hilbert's 10th), and reclaiming dynamically-shared state without GC reintroduces UAF. The no-seam constraint is the binding force — it forbids quarantining that hard relaxed/aliased reasoning behind a trusted boundary, so it must live in the auto-checked fragment where it is undecidable. Every revision re-exposed the same two holes (a concurrently-written atomic head with no Tier-0 token; a device/DMA register the heap model cannot name), confirming the collision rather than a fixable gap.
- **[HARD] Ownership semantics without GC, derived from the proof layer (not a hardcoded borrow checker) ✕ Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Ownership semantics without GC, derived from the proof layer (not a hardcoded borrow checker), Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs), Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land)*
  - surfaced by: Sequential ownership core — for SINGLE-THREADED code only (no concurrency, atomics, or interior mutability), what move/borrow/lifetime discipline gives memory safety without GC, derived from the proof layer rather than a hardcoded borrow checker?
  - Derived ownership and decidable, Rust-cheap checking collide at the control-flow merge point — To DERIVE ownership instead of hardcoding it, capabilities must be first-class/parametric (∀ρ, fractions, PCM resources); merging two such states at a CFG join is then entailment in a general resource logic — Mezzo-heuristic, Iris/RustBelt-undecidable, or Viper-non-principal — i.e. undecidable or proof-demanding. The only merge that is decidable and annotation-free is a fixed syntactic join, which IS the hardcoded borrow checker and still rejects programs Rust accepts. Every finite-lattice compromise fails to encode the needed distinctions (affine-not-Copy, disjoint-mutable partition, non-droppable caps), losing soundness or completeness — exposed concretely by `let r = if b {&x} else {&y}`, split_at_mut yielding two writers, and the loop-header fixpoint with no solution. RustBelt makes the dual explicit: derivability-from-resource-logic is itself an undecidable meta-theorem, i.e. the very seam the design forbids.
- **[HARD] Ownership semantics without GC, derived from the proof layer (not a hardcoded borrow checker) ✕ Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Ownership semantics without GC, derived from the proof layer (not a hardcoded borrow checker), Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs), Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land)*
  - surfaced by: Decidability boundary — precisely which fragment of dependent types is admitted, with the formal argument that it is decidable?
  - Derived sound ownership and decidable proof-free checking collide on real data structures — Sound ownership-without-GC requires a substructural, heap-address-quantified separation logic: linear permissions (no contraction, or `free x; free x` type-checks) carrying unbounded ∀-index footprints `⊛_{i<n} pt(arr[i],1,_)` for slab free lists, Vec<Box<T>>, and intrusive ready-queues. But the layer that makes checking decidable with no user proofs is necessarily contraction-admitting and quantifier-free — so it both duplicates ownership witnesses (double-free) and cannot express those footprints, which sit in the provably undecidable array-property fragment (Bradley–Manna–Sipma) / NP-complete array separation logic (Brotherston). Because the unified layer has no FFI seam or unsafe floor to quarantine the assertion, the obligation cannot be hidden: it must surface as either non-terminating type checking or the ATS2 hand-proof cliff. Mechanically, decidable proof-free checking gives — every revision's decidability lemma died on exactly this configuration.
- **[HARD] Zero-cost abstractions (the proof layer erases at compile time) ✕ Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Zero-cost abstractions (the proof layer erases at compile time), Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs), Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land)*
  - surfaced by: Proof erasure — how are proof witnesses eliminated at compile time with a formal guarantee they leave no runtime trace?
  - Zero-cost erasure needs irrelevant-to-equality witnesses; decidable seam-free checking needs those same witnesses relevant. — A no-trace erasure theorem holds only if erased witnesses are irrelevant to computation, and the sole lever that makes this decidable is definitional proof irrelevance. But in a unified, seam-free language where the spec IS the type system, that same witness is fed to the kernel's equality decision — so making it erasable collapses runtime-distinct values (0≡S n, acquire≡relaxed atomics, Vec n≡Vec m), while keeping it relevant either retains it at runtime (non-zero-cost) or demands undecidable equality (n+m≡m+n). The recurring pattern is index/ownership/weak-memory-ordering data that must be erased for cost yet decides runtime behavior; a single erasure axis (multiplicity, universe, or grade) cannot host it, which is exactly why QTT-0, GraD grade-0, and Rocq RFC #32 split erasure from irrelevance into two orthogonal axes the unification requirement forbids.
- **[HARD] Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs) ✕ Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs), Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land), Zero-cost abstractions (the proof layer erases at compile time)*
  - surfaced by: Unsafe boundary — what does 'unsafe' mean here, and which invariants does crossing it break and then restore?
  - Decidable auto-discharged seam can't restore the open, entangled invariant set soundness demands — A proof-free decidable seam forces unsafe to be a finite, closed lattice of erasable per-location grades, since auto-discharge means looking up a grade. But the invariants crossing unsafe must restore — non-interference, representation validity, dereferenceability, memory coherence — are flow- and value-dependent and provably non-orthogonal (Hansen-Larsen-Askarov: a false-alias assume in the memory dimension discharges a flow obligation), so they cannot be partitioned into independent erasable grades. Concretely, each revision added one grade (Order, then Init/Own, then Valid, then an IFC label) and the next attack rode the invariant still outside the lattice past the seam ungraded — the laundering surviving erasure precisely because zero-cost demands the labels vanish.
- **[HARD] Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs) ✕ Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land)**  <sub>(within failed question)</sub>
  - property at risk: *Decidable type checking (common case needs no user-written proofs), Unified proof/systems layer (no FFI seam between proof-land and systems-land), Zero-cost abstractions (the proof layer erases at compile time)*
  - surfaced by: Interior mutability & weak memory — how are shared-mutable cells, atomics, MMIO/device registers (read-to-clear, write-1-to-clear), and ARM/POWER/RISC-V memory ordering typed, given the sequential ownership core cannot express them?
  - Decidable proof-free checking collides with sound, zero-cost typing of shared-mutable/weak-memory state — Linear ownership makes exclusivity decidable and erasable for free, but every shared-mutable or weak-memory idiom needs an invariant that carries runtime data into itself: pointer disequality for non-reentrancy, impredicative/later-modality protocols for generic Mutex/Atomic, unbounded value-indexed resources for SPSC/free-list loops, and per-agent view closures for IRIW. These are mechanically outside any finite first-order decidable fragment, so forcing the check to stay decidable and proof-free collapses the invariant to a finite lattice that is provably unsound (an atomic initialized to the acquire-sentinel duplicates the unique token; finite per-agent closure certifies a consensus invariant POWER permits to fail) or too weak to pass a token across an acquire-load, an interrupt mask, or a DMA boundary. The only sound, expressive repairs reintroduce a runtime witness flag (breaking zero-cost) or an interactive separation-logic+induction proof (breaking proof-free decidability) — so decidability is the property that must give.
